categories.prompt: Name a video game where you can play as an animal.
categories.scope: Animal protagonists and selectable animal characters count; fictional animal species count.

categories.prompt: Name a video game where you can drive a car or kart.
categories.scope: The driving must be part of the unmodded game, not a fan modification.

categories.prompt: Name a free-to-play PC or console game.
categories.scope: Games with an officially free base version count; a temporary free weekend does not.

categories.prompt: Name a video game you can play with someone on the same screen or console.
categories.scope: Local co-op, split-screen and shared-screen multiplayer count.

categories.prompt: Name a video game with a crafting system.
categories.scope: The player must be able to combine resources into an item in normal gameplay.

categories.prompt: Name a video game where the player can go fishing.
categories.scope: A player-controlled fishing activity counts, including optional minigames.

categories.prompt: Name a villain from a video game.
categories.scope: Named antagonists from any era or platform count; no voice-actor names.

categories.prompt: Name an item that restores health in a video game.
categories.scope: Named consumables, pickups and healing items count; name the actual item.

categories.prompt: Name a named weapon from a video game.
categories.scope: Unique named weapons and established weapon/item names count across all platforms.

categories.prompt: Name a named place or map from a video game.
categories.scope: Named maps, towns, regions and locations count; ordinary real-world cities need a named in-game setting.

categories.prompt: Name a Minecraft mob that can attack a player.
categories.scope: Hostile, neutral and defensive mobs that can attack a player count. Released vanilla Java or Bedrock gameplay; non-mob entities, command-only mobs and passive mounts do not count.

categories.prompt: Name something a player can eat in Minecraft.
categories.scope: Vanilla food items count, including foods with negative effects.

categories.prompt: Name something you can craft using wood, planks or sticks in Minecraft.
categories.scope: Any vanilla recipe that directly uses a log, plank or stick counts.

categories.prompt: Name a location that has appeared on a Fortnite Battle Royale map.
categories.scope: Named locations from any past or present Battle Royale season count.

categories.prompt: Name a Fortnite item that restores health or shields.
categories.scope: Battle Royale consumables from any season count, including vaulted items.

categories.prompt: Name a weapon that has appeared in Fortnite Battle Royale.
categories.scope: Any season counts; ordinary loot, Mythic and vaulted weapons all count.

categories.prompt: Name a character from the Mario games.
categories.scope: Characters from Mario games and their spin-offs count; actor names do not.

categories.prompt: Name one of the original 151 Pokémon.
categories.scope: The original species names count; you do not need to name a special form.

categories.prompt: Name a boss from Elden Ring.
categories.scope: The base game and Shadow of the Erdtree count; common short boss names would be aliases.

categories.prompt: Name a board or card game people can play together offline.
categories.scope: Published games and traditional named games count; video games do not.

categories.prompt: Name a team from the NFL, NBA, MLB, NHL, WNBA or MLS.
categories.scope: Past and present teams from those six leagues count; familiar short team names would be accepted.

categories.prompt: Name an athlete who has played professionally in a team sport.
categories.scope: Men's and women's sports, any country and any era count; no roster-year restriction.

categories.prompt: Name a sport or competitive game played with a ball.
categories.scope: A ball must be part of normal play; variations with their own established names count.

categories.prompt: Name a sport played with a racket, bat, stick or club.
categories.scope: Any one of those implements qualifies; named sport variants count.

categories.prompt: Name a sport or event that has appeared at the modern Olympics.
categories.scope: Summer and Winter Games count, including discontinued events.

categories.prompt: Name an athlete who has won an Olympic gold medal.
categories.scope: Any modern Summer or Winter Games count; team-event gold medals count too.

categories.prompt: Name a brand that makes athletic shoes.
categories.scope: Real sports-footwear brands count, including specialist running and court-shoe brands.

categories.prompt: Name a player position in a team sport.
categories.scope: Named playing positions from any established team sport count; shared names are one answer.

categories.prompt: Name a professional sports team whose name includes an animal.
categories.scope: The team nickname must name an animal or animal group. A city name alone, such as Buffalo, does not count.

categories.prompt: Name a stadium, arena or racetrack used for professional sports.
categories.scope: Named venues anywhere in the world count; past venue names would be aliases.

categories.prompt: Name a piece of equipment an athlete wears.
categories.scope: Protective gear, specialist footwear and worn sporting equipment count; handheld equipment does not.

categories.prompt: Name an athlete featured on a video game's cover or in its title.
categories.scope: An officially released sports game's cover athlete or title namesake qualifies.

categories.prompt: Name a movie that is a sequel to another movie.
categories.scope: Direct sequels count, even if there is no number in the title.

categories.prompt: Name a movie based on a video game.
categories.scope: Released feature films count, including animation; a game based on a movie is the reverse and does not qualify.

categories.prompt: Name a movie with scenes set in outer space.
categories.scope: Some of the story must take place beyond Earth's atmosphere.

categories.prompt: Name an animated movie with talking animal characters.
categories.scope: Animated features and shorts with at least one speaking animal character count, including hybrids with animation. Dialogue through a translation device counts; silent animal sidekicks alone do not.

categories.prompt: Name a superhero movie.
categories.scope: Live action and animation count; heroes from any publisher or original story count.

categories.prompt: Name an animated TV series.
categories.scope: Shows for any audience count, including cartoons, anime and streaming series.

categories.prompt: Name a sitcom.
categories.scope: Live-action and animated situation comedies count; sketch-only shows do not.

categories.prompt: Name a movie or TV character with superpowers.
categories.scope: A named character must have a supernatural or superhuman ability in the story.

categories.prompt: Name a fictional robot.
categories.scope: Robots and droids from films, TV, books or games count; actors and real-world robots do not.

categories.prompt: Name a fictional animal character.
categories.scope: Named animal characters from any published story count; real celebrity pets do not.

categories.prompt: Name an actor who appears in a Marvel Cinematic Universe movie.
categories.scope: Released MCU feature films count; voice and motion-capture performances count too.

categories.prompt: Name a villain from a children's animated TV series.
categories.scope: Named antagonists count even if they sometimes help the heroes.

categories.prompt: Name a fictional city or town from a movie or TV show.
categories.scope: A real place's fictional version qualifies only when it is clearly part of that story's setting.

categories.prompt: Name a horror movie villain or monster.
categories.scope: Named villains, creatures and monster species from horror films count.

categories.prompt: Name a song with a person's name in its title.
categories.scope: Released songs count; the name can be a real person or a fictional person.

categories.prompt: Name a song with a color in its title.
categories.scope: Ordinary color words in released song titles count; color names used as surnames need context.

categories.prompt: Name a musical artist or band with a number in their name.
categories.scope: Numbers written as digits, words or Roman numerals count.

categories.prompt: Name a music group with at least three members.
categories.scope: Bands and vocal groups from any era count; a solo artist's unnamed backing band does not.

categories.prompt: Name a rapper, past or present.
categories.scope: Released professional hip-hop artists count; established stage names would be aliases.

categories.prompt: Name a music festival.
categories.scope: Named public music festivals anywhere in the world count; a one-off concert does not.

categories.prompt: Name a musician known professionally by one name.
categories.scope: An established one-word stage name counts even when their legal name has several words.

categories.prompt: Name a musical instrument played by blowing air into it.
categories.scope: Mouth-blown instruments count, including reed, brass and free-reed instruments.

categories.prompt: Name something sold as a pizza topping.
categories.scope: Established restaurant toppings count worldwide; you do not need to name a pizza brand.

categories.prompt: Name something people put inside a sandwich.
categories.scope: Established sandwich fillings count, including spreads and condiments.

categories.prompt: Name a food commonly cooked by frying.
categories.scope: Named foods and dishes count; a one-off experiment is not enough.

categories.prompt: Name a food commonly served on a stick.
categories.scope: Named foods and established skewer dishes count, including sweets.

categories.prompt: Name a named breakfast food or breakfast dish.
categories.scope: Named breakfast foods and dishes from any country count; plain beverages are separate.

categories.prompt: Name a pasta shape.
categories.scope: Named pasta shapes count; sauces and full dishes are separate.

categories.prompt: Name a named type of bread.
categories.scope: Named breads, rolls and flatbreads count; filling-only variations do not create a new bread.

categories.prompt: Name a candy or chocolate brand.
categories.scope: Brands and named candy products count; ordinary flavor names alone do not.

categories.prompt: Name a fast-food or fast-casual restaurant chain.
categories.scope: Real multi-location restaurant chains count worldwide; local independents do not.

categories.prompt: Name a drink you can order at a coffee shop.
categories.scope: Established drink names count, including non-coffee drinks; every flavor combination would not be a separate answer.

categories.prompt: Name a dish made mainly from potatoes.
categories.scope: Named dishes count when potato is a main ingredient rather than a garnish.

categories.prompt: Name a fruit used in a sweet dessert.
categories.scope: Fresh, dried or cooked fruit in an established dessert qualifies.

categories.prompt: Name an animal that can deliver venom.
categories.scope: Venom must be injected or delivered by a bite, sting or spine; simply being poisonous is different.

categories.prompt: Name an animal that changes color.
categories.scope: Rapid camouflage and seasonal changes both count.

categories.prompt: Name an animal that flies but is not a bird.
categories.scope: Powered flight counts; an animal that only glides does not.

categories.prompt: Name a wild animal that spends time both in water and on land.
categories.scope: The animal must normally use both habitats, not merely survive a brief swim.

categories.prompt: Name a kind of shark or ray.
categories.scope: Established groups and species count; familiar common names would be accepted.

categories.prompt: Name an animal that lays eggs.
categories.scope: Named animal groups and species qualify; males do not have to lay the eggs themselves.

categories.prompt: Name an animal that is active at night.
categories.scope: Normally nocturnal or regularly night-active animals count; occasional unusual behavior does not.

categories.prompt: Name an animal people have used for work or transport.
categories.scope: Documented domesticated or trained working animals count, past or present.

categories.prompt: Name a plant people eat.
categories.scope: Named edible plants count, including those eaten for fruit, leaves, roots or seeds; fungi are separate.

categories.prompt: Name a plant that has thorns, spines or prickles.
categories.scope: The sharp growth can be on any ordinary part of the plant; edible plants count too.

categories.prompt: Name a named object in our Solar System.
categories.scope: Planets, dwarf planets, moons, named asteroids and named comets count; stars beyond the Sun do not.

categories.prompt: Name something people use to measure things.
categories.scope: Named measuring instruments count; the quantity being measured can be distance, time, temperature or something else.

categories.prompt: Name a machine or device that uses an electric motor.
categories.scope: The motor can be internal and does not need to move the entire device.

categories.prompt: Name something that produces visible light.
categories.scope: Natural sources and human-made devices count; a reflector alone does not.

categories.prompt: Name a weather event or weather condition.
categories.scope: Common and established technical names count; fictional weather does not.

categories.prompt: Name a body part a typical human has more than one of.
categories.scope: Named bones, organs and body parts count; ordinary singular names would be accepted.

categories.prompt: Name a chemical element used in everyday products.
categories.scope: There must be a documented consumer, industrial or medical use; exact product names are not required.

categories.prompt: Name a real vehicle that can fly.
categories.scope: Real vehicle types and named models count; fictional vehicles and craft that only float on water do not.

categories.prompt: Name a landmark people can visit.
categories.scope: Named natural or human-made visitor landmarks count, including ruins.

categories.prompt: Name a country made up entirely of islands.
categories.scope: Island countries and countries sharing an island count; Australia explicitly counts.

categories.prompt: Name an amusement park or theme-park resort.
categories.scope: Real parks and resort complexes count worldwide; familiar resort names would be accepted.

categories.prompt: Name a city that has hosted the modern Olympics.
categories.scope: Summer and Winter hosts count; ancient host cities alone do not.

categories.prompt: Name a food named after a place.
categories.scope: The place name must appear in an established food or dish name.

categories.prompt: Name a country whose national flag contains a star.
categories.scope: A visible star on the official national flag qualifies; tiny stars inside a coat of arms count too.

categories.prompt: Name something students bring to school.
categories.scope: Physical items brought for an ordinary school day count; people and pets do not.

categories.prompt: Name an item used in a bathroom.
categories.scope: Established bathroom, bathing, grooming and hygiene items count.

categories.prompt: Name something people open using a key or a code.
categories.scope: Physical objects and devices count; the code can be a password or combination.

categories.prompt: Name an everyday object with wheels.
categories.scope: Ordinary objects and vehicles count; named types count without needing a brand.

categories.prompt: Name a way to pay for something without physical cash.
categories.scope: Payment methods, payment networks and named payment services count.

categories.prompt: Name something that can be controlled with a remote.
categories.scope: A real consumer product type with a handheld or app-based remote qualifies.

categories.prompt: Name something you can wear that has a button, zipper or buckle.
categories.scope: Clothes, footwear, accessories and protective wear count.

categories.prompt: Name something people can borrow from a public library.
categories.scope: Items must actually be offered by a public library somewhere; Library of Things collections count.

categories.prompt: Name an item used for sewing or mending clothes.
categories.scope: Hand-sewing, machine-sewing and dressmaking tools and supplies count. A finished garment alone is not sewing equipment.

categories.prompt: Name a tool or piece of equipment used for gardening.

categories.prompt: Name an item or product used to wash, dry or care for laundry.
categories.scope: Laundry appliances, supplies, stain treatments and clothes-care tools count, as do named product types and established laundry-product brands, including historical ones. A garment itself is not a laundry supply.

categories.prompt: Name an object that commonly has a hinge.
categories.scope: A common hinged version of the object must exist. Sliding or roll-up versions do not prevent a genuinely hinged object from counting.

categories.prompt: Name a hand tool or utensil used to prepare or serve food.
categories.scope: Kitchen hand tools, utensils, serving implements and nonpowered cookware count. Small measuring tools used in food preparation also count. Large powered appliances and foods do not qualify.

categories.prompt: Name a block an Enderman can pick up in Minecraft.
categories.scope: The actual block-pickup rule counts, including flowers. Endermen may pick up only certain blocks even if the player can carry other blocks. Official Java 26.3 recipe, tag or component data defines the inventory; modded behavior does not count.

categories.prompt: Name a flower or flowering block found in Minecraft.
categories.scope: Flower items and blocks count, including tall flowers and Nether-compatible flowers. Named crops and saplings do not become flowers merely because they are plants. Official Java 26.3 recipe, tag or component data defines the inventory; modded behavior does not count.

categories.prompt: Name an item you can catch by fishing in Minecraft.
categories.scope: Fish, junk and treasure in the ordinary fishing loot tables count. Items merely carried by nearby mobs do not. Official Java 26.3 recipe, tag or component data defines the inventory; modded behavior does not count.

categories.prompt: Name an item or block a furnace recipe can produce in Minecraft.
categories.scope: Give the output, rather than the input, of an ordinary furnace smelting or cooking recipe. Official Java 26.3 recipe, tag or component data defines the inventory; modded behavior does not count.

categories.prompt: Name an item that can be used as furnace fuel in Minecraft.
categories.scope: Items actually accepted in the fuel slot count, rather than anything that merely looks flammable. Their fuel value need not be the same. Official Java 26.3 recipe, tag or component data defines the inventory; modded behavior does not count.

categories.prompt: Name a Minecraft block you can strip, scrape or unwax by using an axe on it.
categories.scope: This asks for the right-click/use action. Merely chopping or breaking a block does not qualify. Both stripping wood and removing copper oxidation or wax count. Official Java 26.3 recipe, tag or component data defines the inventory; modded behavior does not count.

categories.prompt: Name a combat sport or established martial art.
categories.scope: Named competitive fighting disciplines and established martial arts count, including forms practiced without full-contact competition. Fictional styles do not count.

categories.prompt: Name a sport or recognized sporting discipline played on snow or ice.
categories.scope: Established ice and snow sports and competitive disciplines count. A sport merely played during the winter on an ordinary indoor court does not qualify.

categories.prompt: Name a player who has won the NBA regular-season MVP award.
categories.scope: Winners of the main NBA regular-season Most Valuable Player award through the 2025–26 season count. Finals, All-Star and other leagues' MVP awards are different.

categories.prompt: Name a quarterback who started and won a Super Bowl.
categories.scope: The quarterback must have started a winning Super Bowl, through Super Bowl LX in February 2026. Winning a ring as a backup alone does not count.

categories.prompt: Name one of the 88 official constellations.
categories.scope: Official IAU constellation names count. Recognized common names such as Capricorn and the Great Bear are accepted. Asterisms such as the Big Dipper are only parts of constellations.

categories.prompt: Name a playable hero in Dota 2.
categories.scope: The complete official playable hero roster in the October 25, 2026 snapshot counts. Items, cosmetics and non-playable creeps are not heroes.

categories.prompt: Name a playable hero in Overwatch.
categories.scope: The full official Overwatch roster in the October 25, 2026 snapshot counts, including heroes introduced while it was called Overwatch 2. Skins and unplayable story characters do not.

categories.prompt: Name a playable fighter in Super Smash Bros. Ultimate.
categories.scope: All base-game, Echo and DLC fighters count. Pokémon Trainer's three Pokémon, the three Mii fighting styles, and Pyra/Mythra count separately. Alternate costumes share the original fighter's answer; Assist Trophies do not count.

categories.prompt: Name a Legendary or Mythical Pokémon.
categories.scope: Species classified as Legendary or Mythical in the pinned PokéAPI data count. Forms share their species' answer identity. Pseudo-Legendary is a fan label and does not make a species Legendary.

categories.prompt: Name a music act known as a duo.
categories.scope: Current and historical musical duos count. Ordinary backing musicians do not change a two-person act into a larger group. Two solo artists who collaborated once are not automatically a named duo.

categories.prompt: Name a real mountain range.
categories.scope: Named ranges, chains, mountain systems and subranges count, anywhere in the world. A single peak by itself is not a range.

categories.prompt: Name a real museum.
categories.scope: Named museums and museum complexes count, including historical institutions. Multiple institutions with the same name share an answer identity. A type of museum or a fictional museum is not a named real institution.

categories.prompt: Name a record label or record company.
categories.scope: Real current and historical record labels, imprints and record companies count. A publisher, streaming platform or music store is not automatically a record label.

categories.prompt: Name a real DJ or DJ act, past or present.
categories.scope: Real DJs and billed DJ duos or groups count, including people known for presenting recorded music on radio. Being a singer or producer alone does not make someone a DJ. Fictional story DJs and unrelated musical groups do not count.

categories.prompt: Name a musician known for playing drums.
categories.scope: Real musicians known for playing drums count, including multi-instrumentalists and percussionists with a documented drum-playing career. An unrelated band member does not become a drummer just because the band has one.

categories.prompt: Name a musical instrument with a keyboard.
categories.scope: Recognized keyboard-instrument types and documented named keyboard instruments or models count. Keys and buttons form the musical playing interface; having ordinary valves or attaching an external controller does not automatically qualify another instrument.

categories.prompt: Name a real named canal.
categories.scope: Named canals, shipping channels and recognized artificial waterways count worldwide, including disused historical ones. Natural rivers are not automatically canals.

categories.prompt: Name a real waterfall.
categories.scope: Named waterfalls and recognized waterfall complexes count worldwide. Multiple real falls with the same name share an answer identity. Fictional falls and generic words such as waterfall do not count.

categories.prompt: Name a driver who has competed in Formula One.
categories.scope: Drivers in the complete Jolpica/Ergast Formula One World Championship driver inventory count, including historical entrants and the Indianapolis 500 when it was part of that championship. A real surname can identify a valid driver; invented initials and racing three-letter codes do not count as names.

categories.prompt: Name a fictional detective.
categories.scope: Named fictional professional detectives and amateur sleuths count across books, comics, film, TV and games. A character must actually investigate cases; merely appearing in a mystery does not qualify.

categories.prompt: Name a fictional pirate.
categories.scope: Named fictional sea, air and space pirates count, including characters who were pirates earlier in their story. A smuggler, sailor or marine is not automatically a pirate.

categories.prompt: Name a princess from fiction.
categories.scope: Characters who are, were, or are explicitly known as princesses count, along with the official Disney Princess lineup. A character does not qualify simply by being female, wearing a crown or appearing in a Disney movie.

categories.prompt: Name a named vehicle from fiction.
categories.scope: Named fictional vehicles, ships and vehicle models count across film, TV, books, comics and games, including living vehicle characters. Generic words such as car or spaceship, and individual parts that are not vehicles, do not count.

categories.prompt: Name a school or college from fiction.
categories.scope: Named fictional schools, colleges, universities and training academies count across books, TV, film, comics and games. A real school does not qualify just because a fictional story mentions it.

categories.prompt: Name a heist movie.
categories.scope: Films built around a robbery, theft, con or organized caper count, including comedies, animated movies and shorts. Television series, directors and a film with only an unrelated passing theft do not automatically count.

categories.prompt: Name a movie involving time travel or a time loop.
categories.scope: Films in which characters travel through time or experience a repeating time loop count, including animated movies and shorts. Ordinary flashbacks, dreams about the past and a futuristic setting alone do not count.

categories.prompt: Name a kind of owl.
categories.scope: Owl species and established named groups count, including recently extinct species in the source taxonomy. Common names and scientific names count. An owlet-nightjar or a nighthawk is not an owl.

categories.prompt: Name a kind of parrot.
categories.scope: Parrot species and established named groups count, including recently extinct species in the source taxonomy. Common and scientific names count. Pet colour mutations share their species identity; a bird is not a parrot just because its name contains that word.

categories.prompt: Name a kind of penguin.
categories.scope: Species in the eBird/Clements penguin order and established common group names count. English or scientific names count. Puffins and auks are different kinds of bird.

categories.prompt: Name a kind of bat.
categories.scope: Living and recently extinct species in the Mammal Diversity Database, plus established named bat groups, count. Common names and documented scientific names count. A flying fox is a bat; a flying squirrel is not. Prehistoric fossil-only species are outside this current-species inventory.

categories.prompt: Name a type of rock.
categories.scope: Recognized geological rock names, rock families and established natural stone varieties count. Common and scientific rock names are accepted. Individual minerals, chemical elements, whole mountains and manufactured building products are not rock types.

categories.prompt: Name a type or named product of dairy cheese.
categories.scope: Named dairy cheeses, traditional cheese families and named processed-cheese products count. Different names for the same cheese share one answer. A dairy animal, plain milk, a manufacturer with no named cheese product, and a complete meal merely containing cheese do not count.

categories.prompt: Name a kind of flatbread.
categories.scope: Recognized flatbread types, named regional breads and flatbread dishes count, including leavened and unleavened types. Ordinary sandwich loaves, toppings and ingredients alone do not count.

categories.prompt: Name a pancake style or a named pancake dish.
categories.scope: Recognized sweet and savory pancake styles and named pancake dishes count, including potato pancakes and international griddle-batter breads. A topping alone, an unrelated pastry, or simply the category word pancake does not count.

categories.prompt: Name a stew or a named stew dish.
categories.scope: Named stews, braised one-pot dishes and recognized ingredient-based stew styles count. Soups that are also conventionally served as stews count; a raw ingredient, drink or dry standalone food does not.

categories.prompt: Name a web browser.
categories.scope: Actual web-browser products and families count, including historical, mobile and text browsers. A search engine, rendering engine, extension, website or operating system alone is not a browser.

categories.prompt: Name a cloud type, form or recognized cloud feature.
categories.scope: Cloud genera, species, varieties and recognized cloud features count, along with established common names such as lenticular cloud, contrail and fog at ground level. Weather events, precipitation and a blue sky alone do not count.
